subject: English
passage: In Natalie Sullivan's exhibition Tokens of an Unwritten Guild, each one of the hundreds of commemorative medallions—arranged in neat rows within the velvet-lined vitrines that line the gallery's central corridor, on the oak pedestals that cluster near the archways, and on the plaster walls that flank the entryway— ______ an inscription that cannot be read. Fabricated by Sullivan, the inscriptions appear authoritative and solemn, resembling the insignia of old trade fraternities yet resisting every attempt at translation.
prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Choice B is the best answer. The convention tested is subject-verb agreement and tense consistency. The singular verb 'carries' agrees with the singular subject 'each one of the hundreds of commemorative medallions'—although the lengthy em-dash parenthetical contains several plural nouns ('vitrines,' 'pedestals,' 'walls'), the grammatical subject is the singular pronoun 'each one.' The simple present tense 'carries' is also consistent with the other present-tense verbs and participles in the passage ('appear,' 'resembling,' 'resisting'), which describe the ongoing characteristics of the exhibition.
